classification.difficultyReason: Construct a vector difference from ungridded directed segments with separate tails.

spec.description: Separate tails; a points upwards left and b is longer and points upwards right. Coordinates reconstruct the visible proportions and are not numerical givens.
spec.mathematics: Two unmeasured free vectors with undertilded labels.

answer.short: An arrow pointing gently upwards to the right, as shown.
answer.worked: Translate the two given vectors to a common tail without changing their lengths or directions. The vector from the tip of $\underset{\sim}{a}$ to the tip of $\underset{\sim}{b}$ represents $\underset{\sim}{b}-\underset{\sim}{a}$.

spec.sourceRegion: Question 5 supplied resultant and authored construction
spec.description: Translate the original vectors to a common tail and draw the resultant from the tip of a to the tip of b. Blue distinguishes the constructed difference.
spec.mathematics: The tip-to-tip displacement is b minus a and points gently upwards right.
